hypothesis: The full-text transposition search recovers every known-key control up to a ciphertext-equivalent rotation and exceeds the matched complete-search shuffle null on QTXMA.
refuted_by: A known-key control is recovered neither exactly nor as a rotation that some searched key enciphers to the identical ciphertext, or the target maximum fails complete-search calibration.
notes: This is a bounded smoke experiment, not an exhaustive double-transposition exclusion.
Only order-sensitive n-grams are optimized: Phase 6 uses the bootstrap scorer and Phase 7 substitutes published 1941 counts. Monograms are excluded because transposition preserves them.
Candidate keys are selected by scoring each complete proposed plaintext. Any prefix or suffix statistics are descriptive only.
The target widths are a small first-pass set centered on short hand-cipher keys and do not include every historically possible rectangle.
A score-only candidate is not an accepted break without coherent plaintext, historical procedure, and independent reproduction.
The candidate suffix is descriptive only; no independent held-out claim is made from it.
revision_rationale: The v2 run failed the independent solved-message 5x7 control because its acceptance rule credited a rotated recovery only when a stage width divides the message length. The 76-letter control has a one-letter ragged final row at width 5, which lets the first-stage order [4,1,0,2,3] encipher the plaintext rotated by one character to exactly the same ciphertext as the known order [3,0,4,1,2]; the search selected that equivalent key. The earlier reading of this as a row-filling convention mismatch is withdrawn: construction and untransposition agree. v3 credits a rotation only when some key in the searched widths enciphers it to the identical control ciphertext, computed exactly per control. The rule is stricter where divisibility over-admitted: the 148-letter primary control now admits offset zero only instead of 37 offsets.
